skills.name: Slaying

skills.name: Hunting

skills.name: Farming

skills.desc: Turning raw catches and crops into proper meals.

skills.name: Agility

charms.name: Hearth Charm
charms.desc: Restores 8 health. An old bedside blessing, said over salt and a bilberry.
charms.words: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, bless the bed that I lie on.

charms.name: Rowan Ward
charms.desc: Takes 30% off the damage you take for 30 seconds. Rowan has warded doorways for centuries.
charms.words: Rowan tree and red thread put the witches to their speed.

charms.name: Boggart-bane
charms.desc: For a minute, you deal double damage to boggarts.
charms.words: Salt on the doorstep, light in the hall, no boggart of yours shall come here at all.

quests.name: Lights for Manchester
quests.intro: A new face! Since Mr Arkwright's mill went up on Miller Street, this town never sleeps, and my lamps never stay lit. Boggarts have been at the lamp posts again. Fetch me some timber, make yourself a sword, and see off a few of the creatures.
quests.outro: You'll do nicely. Here's your pay, and some copper toward a lantern of your own.

quests.name: Lights on the Moors
quests.intro: North of here the road runs up to the Highland moors. Lights dance there at night: will-o'-the-wisps, leading travellers into the bogs. Bring me 3 wisp-light shards and I'll know you can look after yourself. Carry a lantern, and if it goes badly, your Hearth Lantern will bring you home.
quests.outro: Back in one piece, and with your pockets glowing. Take this token, and my thanks.

quests.name: Supper for the Mill Hands
quests.intro: The mill hands work fourteen hours and come out starving, and I've nothing on the griddle. Take this rod and tinderbox. There's herring rising off the coast west of town: catch some, get a fire going, and cook them up. My range by the market will do if the wind's against you.
quests.outro: Lovely, and hardly burnt at all. Here's a few coppers for your trouble.

steps.text: Light a campfire with a log

quests.name: Salt and Rowan
quests.intro: Boggarts, wisps, worse besides. The mill-owners laugh at charms, but they still hang rowan over their doors. Take this wand and a pouch of salt: equip the wand and it'll throw will-light at anything that troubles you. See off a few boggarts with it, then show me you can work a Hearth Charm.
quests.outro: There. You've the knack for it. Keep your salt dry, and come back when you want more.

steps.text: Work a Hearth Charm (it's on your hotbar)

quests.name: The Squire's Hares
quests.intro: Hares in the squire's turnips again. The game laws say only gentlemen may take them, but the squire says I may deputise. Take these snares: set them on open ground out in the fields and come back for them. Or chase the beasts down yourself, if you're quick.
quests.outro: Four hares and the hides besides. The squire will be pleased, and I'll not ask where you learned to snare like that.

quests.name: Potatoes for the Poorhouse
quests.intro: The poorhouse on Cumberland Street feeds three hundred souls, and the parish pays a pittance. Here's seed potatoes: plant them in the allotment soil behind me, wait for them to come up, and bake a few for the poor folk.
quests.outro: Good, honest work. Keep the spare seed, and come back when you want oats or cabbages.

quests.name: The Magistrate's Warrant
quests.intro: Josiah Rawcliffe, Justice of the Peace. The county pays for every creature that troubles honest folk, and I sign the warrants. Prove yourself on the boggarts outside town, and I'll have regular work for you. There's an old one in Boggart Hole Clough that nobody has managed to shift; maybe one day.
quests.outro: Good. From now on, ask me for a warrant whenever you want one. And keep your hands out of other people's pockets; I do hear about it.

npcs.name: Mabel Hartley, Lamplighter
lines: They've lit Philips and Lee's mill over in Salford with gas, they say. One day every street will glow like it.
Mr Blake the poet writes of "dark Satanic Mills". I'd rather they were well-lit ones.

npcs.name: Bertram Oakes, Shudehill Market
lines: Bilberries! Planks! Lanterns for the moors! I buy logs and ore too.
Coal's been cheap since the Duke of Bridgewater's canal opened in 1761. Barges bring it in from Worsley.

npcs.name: Hannah Leigh, Fishwife
lines: Herring off the coast, salmon when they run up the Mersey, and cod if you go deep enough. A rod and patience, that's all.
They say the Liverpool boats bring in more herring in a morning than Manchester eats in a week.

npcs.name: Nance Clegg, Cunning-woman
lines: Salt on the step and rowan over the door. My grandmother swore by it, and no boggart ever crossed her threshold.
A cunning-woman finds lost things, cures warts and keeps the dark at bay. The magistrate pretends not to know me.

npcs.name: Abel Fothergill, Gamekeeper
lines: Hares by the field gate, grouse up toward the moors, and red deer off to the north-east. Deer need a steady hand.
Poaching's a hanging matter if the magistrate's in a mood. Snares are fine when the squire allows it, mind.

npcs.name: Jonas Ogden, Smallholder
lines: Potatoes keep a family alive through winter. Oats too, if you've a pot to boil them in.
Plant and walk away; they grow whether you watch or not.

npcs.name: Josiah Rawcliffe, Magistrate
lines: The Riot Act is read, the warrant is signed, and the creature is dealt with. That is how a county is kept.
Some say the boggart of the Clough is older than the parish. I say it is overdue a warrant.

npcs.name: Ottiwell Kershaw, Watchman
lines: The moors are no shame to avoid, friend. Nobody will think less of you for staying by the fire.
Shakespeare had Puck do what the wisps do: "Mislead night-wanderers, laughing at their harm."
